title: Quebec expressions set 2
goal: By the end of this lesson you can understand and use a second set of everyday Quebec expressions (avoir de la misère, niaiser, c'est plate, bon matin, avoir hâte, jaser, chialer, capoter and more), and know their standard equivalents.

body: These expressions are part of everyday spoken Quebec French, used by everyone from teenagers to grandparents. Most are **informal**: perfect with friends, colleagues and neighbours, but in a formal letter or job interview, use the standard equivalent.
Each one fits into grammar you already know: you can conjugate them, put them in the passé composé, use them with pronouns.
**Avoir de la misère (à + infinitive)** = to have a hard time (doing something). Standard: *avoir du mal à*. *J'ai de la misère à me lever le matin.*
**C'est plate** = it's boring, or that's too bad. Standard: *c'est ennuyant / ennuyeux* (boring), *c'est dommage* (too bad). *Le film était plate.* *Tu ne viens pas? C'est plate!*
**Être écœuré (de)** = to be fed up (with). Standard: *en avoir assez*. **Chialer** = to complain, whine. Standard: *se plaindre*.

**Niaiser** = to kid around, tease, or waste time. *Arrête de niaiser!* (Stop fooling around!) *Tu me niaises?* (Are you kidding me?) *Se faire niaiser* = to get fooled / be made fun of. Related: *niaiseux* = silly, dumb.
**Jaser** = to chat (standard: *bavarder, discuter*): *On a jasé toute la soirée.*
**Capoter** = to freak out, go crazy (with stress or excitement): *J'ai capoté quand j'ai vu le prix!* *Capoter sur* = to be crazy about: *Je capote sur ce groupe.*
**Achaler** = to bother, pester (standard: *déranger, embêter*): *Arrête de m'achaler!*
**Bon matin!** = Good morning! Common in Quebec as a cheerful greeting (in France you'd just say *bonjour*). It's widely used and accepted.

**Avoir hâte (de / que)** = to look forward to, can't wait. It's standard French, but Quebecers use it constantly: *J'ai hâte aux vacances! J'ai hâte de te voir!* Note the Quebec *avoir hâte à + noun*.
**Ça a pas d'allure!** = That's ridiculous / that makes no sense. Standard: *ça n'a pas de sens, c'est ridicule*.

examples.fr: J'ai de la misère à comprendre mon nouveau voisin.
examples.en: I have trouble understanding my new neighbour.
examples.note: avoir de la misère à + infinitive

examples.fr: Elle a eu de la misère à trouver un stationnement.
examples.en: She had a hard time finding a parking spot.
examples.note: passé composé: a eu de la misère

examples.fr: Le cours était plate, je me suis endormi.
examples.en: The class was boring, I fell asleep.

examples.fr: Arrête de niaiser, on est en retard!
Tu me niaises? Tu as gagné à la loterie?
examples.en: Are you kidding me? You won the lottery?
Good morning! Did you sleep well?

examples.fr: On a jasé pendant deux heures au téléphone.
examples.en: We chatted for two hours on the phone.

examples.fr: Il chiale toujours contre la météo.
examples.en: He's always complaining about the weather.

examples.fr: Je suis écœuré de la neige!
examples.en: I'm fed up with the snow!

examples.fr: Mes enfants capotent sur ce jeu vidéo.
examples.en: My kids are crazy about this video game.

examples.fr: J'ai capoté quand j'ai vu la facture.
examples.en: I freaked out when I saw the bill.

examples.fr: Trois heures d'attente? Ça a pas d'allure!

examples.en: Don't act dumb! / Don't be silly!

quebec.intro: This whole week is the Quebec layer. Here are the four headline expressions from the roadmap side by side with their standard equivalents. All four are informal except 'bon matin', which is perfectly polite.

items.qc: J'ai de la misère à dormir.
items.note: informal; very common at every age

items.std: Arrête de faire l'idiot! / Tu plaisantes?
items.qc: Arrête de niaiser! / Tu me niaises?
items.en: Stop fooling around! / Are you kidding me?

items.note: polite and common in Quebec; unusual in France

drills.q: 'J'ai de la misère à me concentrer' means…
drills.why: Avoir de la misère à = avoir du mal à.
Niaiser = to fool around, waste time.

drills.q: Which is the standard equivalent of 'jaser'?

drills.en: I can't wait to see you!

drills.q: Il a eu de la ___ à trouver un appartement. (trouble)
drills.en: He had trouble finding an apartment.

drills.q: Arrête de m'___, je suis occupé! (bother)

drills.en: He's always complaining about his boss.
I can't wait for the holidays!

drills.a: On a jasé toute la soirée.

drills.en: I'm fed up with the snow.
drills.a: Je suis écœuré de la neige.

vocab.ex: J'ai de la misère à dormir.

vocab.en: to fool around, kid, tease, waste time
to look forward to, can't wait
to freak out; (sur) to be crazy about

vocab.ex: Ce prix-là, ça a pas d'allure!

pron.tip: mi-ZÈR; in Quebec the è is often long and open: [mi-zaèr].
[plat], rhymes with 'pat': the final t is pronounced.
sa-a-pâ-da-LUR, the two a's are both said.
jé-ÂT, long back â; the h is silent.

dialogue.en: Good morning, Julie! How's it going?

dialogue.fr: Bof. J'ai eu de la misère à me lever. Pis le métro était en panne.
dialogue.en: Meh. I had trouble getting up. And the metro was broken down.
Oh no, that's too bad! Again?

dialogue.fr: Oui, chu écœurée. Une heure pour venir ici, ça a pas d'allure!
dialogue.en: Yes, I'm fed up. An hour to get here, that's ridiculous!

dialogue.fr: Je te comprends. Mais j'ai une bonne nouvelle: le party de bureau est vendredi!
dialogue.en: I get it. But I have good news: the office party is Friday!

dialogue.fr: Tu me niaises? Je pensais que c'était annulé!
dialogue.en: Are you kidding me? I thought it was cancelled!

dialogue.fr: Non, non. Et il y aura un karaoké.
dialogue.en: No, no. And there will be karaoke.
I'm so excited! I can't wait!

questions.q: How does Julie feel at the end?

speak.prompt: Say three things you have trouble doing in French, using avoir de la misère à.
speak.model: J'ai de la misère à comprendre les films. J'ai de la misère à parler vite. J'ai de la misère à rouler mes r.

speak.prompt: Greet a colleague on Monday Quebec style, complain about something, then say what you're looking forward to.
speak.model: Bon matin! Chu écœuré du trafic, c'est plate. Mais j'ai hâte à la fin de semaine!

speak.prompt: A friend tells you surprising news. React with two Quebec expressions.

write.prompt: Write a 5–6 sentence text message to a Quebec friend about your week, using at least five expressions from this lesson. Then rewrite one sentence in standard French.
write.model: Salut! Ma semaine était pas mal plate. J'ai eu de la misère à finir mon projet, pis mon boss m'a achalé tous les jours. Chu écœuré! Mais samedi, on va jaser autour d'un feu au chalet. J'ai tellement hâte! (Standard: J'ai eu du mal à finir mon projet.)

quiz.q: Standard French for 'avoir de la misère à' is…
quiz.why: Both mean to have trouble doing something.
Widely used in Quebec; in France people say bonjour.
Capoter sur = to be crazy about.

quiz.q: Which expression would you avoid in a job interview?
options: Chu écœuré de mon ancienne job.
quiz.why: Chu écœuré is very informal (and negative!).

options: I'm in a hurry for Christmas
quiz.why: Avoir hâte à + noun = look forward to.
